entry.title: FRB 20210601A: Extreme Temporal Clustering in a Repeating Fast Radio Burst Source as Evidence for a Hidden Class of Episodic Repeaters
entry.summary: Population studies of fast radio burst (FRB) repetition typically model sources using a single distribution of steady, time-averaged burst rates, yet individual sources show significant departures from this assumption. Here we present FRB 20210601A, a source discovered by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment FRB project (CHIME/FRB) that represents the most extreme such departure yet identified. The source produced at least nine bursts within a single 106.5 s interval -- the highest instantaneous burst rate yet reported from a repeating FRB source at $\gtrsim 2$ Jy ms fluences -- yet remained otherwise undetected despite $\sim 320$ hr of exposure spanning 7 yr. The active interval occurred while the source was in a side-lobe of the CHIME/FRB digitized beams, implying an instantaneous burst rate $\gtrsim2.3\times$ higher ($\gtrsim$ 21 bursts) at main-lobe sensitivity. The source's intense, brief burst storm flanked by apparent quiescence despite substantial exposure is unique among the CHIME/FRB repeater sample, although its burst morphology, excess dispersion measure ($\rm{DM_{excess}} \sim 360$ pc cm$^{-3}$), Faraday rotation measure ($|\rm{RM_{excess}}| \sim 150-170$ rad m$^{-2}$), and temporal scattering ($τ\lesssim 0.37$ ms at 600 MHz) are otherwise typical. Modeling a population of episodically active repeaters (i.e., short burst storms separated by long recurrence times) and accounting for declination-dependent exposure, we forecast $\sim1-4$ additional source discoveries similar to FRB 20210601A over the next decade of CHIME/FRB operations, corresponding to a CHIME/FRB-detectable population of $9^{+200}_{-8}$ sources (68% credible interval). These results demonstrate that highly episodic repeaters could constitute a selection-biased but detectable component of the FRB population, possibly reflecting distinct magnetospheric states or triggering mechanisms.

entry.title: Spectral Properties of X-Ray Flares in Gamma-Ray Bursts
entry.summary: We conducted a systematic spectral analysis of the X-ray flares of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) observed by Swift/X-ray Telescope from 2005 April to 2015 March. The sample includes 521 flares from 206 GRBs. The GRBs cover the three subtypes: X-ray flashes (XRFs), X-ray-rich GRBs (XRRs), and classical GRBs (C-GRBs). We used a simple power-law model to fit the spectra during the flares, as well as to fit the preflare and postflare afterglow emissions, and obtained the parameters such as photon index and intrinsic hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm H}$). By comparing the spectral characteristics of flares, prompt emission, and afterglow emission, and analyzing the temporal evolution of the X-ray flare spectra, we obtained the following main conclusions. (1) The spectrum during the flare phase is significantly harder than that of the preflare and postflare phases, while there is no obvious difference in the spectrum between the preflare and postflare phases. (2) The intrinsic $N_{\rm H}$ shows no significant change between the preflare and flare phases, but significantly decreases after the flare. (3) The overall X-ray flare spectra are softer than those of the prompt emission. (4) For GRBs with multiple flares, the photon index softens with increasing flare peak time. (5) The X-ray flare spectra in XRFs are softer than those in C-GRBs. These results support the origin of X-ray flares being from the internal shock radiation driven by the late activity of the GRB central engine.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)

entry.title: Possible Microscopic source of torsion
entry.summary: Axial fermionic interactions connect vacuum condensation with torsionful back- grounds. We consider a quartic spin spin interaction whose mean field reduction yields a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian. Its diagonalisation defines a particle and antiparticle condensate, while self consistency determines whether the vacuum devel- ops a non zero axial current. Cutoff, fluctuation and energy conditions delimit the validity of the approximation. When torsion couples to spin, this axial expectation value can provide a microscopic source for an axial torsion background. We then consider mixed Dirac fields on such a background. In the explicit neutrino analysis, metric curvature is neglected while torsion modifies the flavour Bogoliubov coeffi- cients, producing spin dependent oscillation frequencies, condensate densities and CP asymmetries.

entry.title: Graph-Recurrent Learning of Emergent Collective Dynamics
entry.summary: Collective ordering in correlated electron systems emerges from microscopic dynamics, yet the evolution of observable textures need not admit a closed, memoryless description. We introduce a graph-recurrent neural network (GRNN) framework that learns such emergent dynamics directly from trajectories without specifying microscopic equations of motion. The framework integrates gated recurrent memory with graph message passing: local hidden states encode information beyond the instantaneous observables, while spatial coupling allows this information to propagate between sites. The observable and hidden fields evolve jointly through a shared local rule, providing a scalable representation of dynamics with spatial interactions and temporal memory. We demonstrate this framework on the emergent dynamics of charge-density-wave order in the semiclassical Holstein model, successfully reproducing temporal and spatial correlations and dynamical scaling during domain coarsening. By learning finite-time evolution directly, the GRNN offers a route to efficient, data-driven descriptions of collective dynamics with unresolved microscopic degrees of freedom.

entry.title: Stability, Tidal Deformability, and Statistical Constraints of Anisotropic Compact Stars with a Generalized Polytropic Equation of State : Modelling Observation with Buchdahl Space-Time
entry.summary: An anisotropic compact star model is constructed within the framework of general relativity by combining the Buchdahl space-time with a generalized polytropic equation of state. The model parameters are constrained through Darmois-Israel junction conditions by matching interior geometry smoothly with exterior Schwarzschild space-time. The proposed framework is applied to thirty-eight observed compact star candidates spanning a broad range of masses and radii. Regular and physically acceptable distributions of the energy density, radial pressure, tangential pressure, enclosed mass, anisotropy and gravitational redshift are obtained throughout the stellar interior. Energy density and pressure components are found to decrease outward, while the enclosed mass and gravitational redshift are found to increase monotonically towards the stellar surface. The radial pressure is required to vanish at the boundary, thereby determining the estimated stellar radius. The anisotropy is found to provide an additional outward contribution that supports the stellar configurations against gravitational collapse. The physical acceptability of the model is examined through the Zeldovich condition, radial adiabatic index, causality conditions and Herrera cracking criterion. Hydrostatic equilibrium is achieved through the balance among gravitational, hydrostatic and anisotropic forces. The tidal response is also investigated, and an inverse relation between the estimated mass and dimensionless tidal deformability is obtained. The calculated configurations span \(2.88\lesssim M_{\rm Est}/M_\odot\lesssim3.23\) and yield \(22.55\lesssimΛ\lesssim68.38\). MCMC analysis provides statistically constrained compactness and tidal parameters. Overall, a physically viable description of anisotropic compact stars is obtained.

entry.title: Unitarity methods for Magnus amplitudes
entry.summary: Magnus amplitudes refer to the matrix elements of the logarithm of the $S$-matrix. Modern unitarity methods construct cut-constructible parts of scattering amplitudes without directly invoking Feynman diagrams, offering an efficient way of obtaining loop integrands for scattering amplitudes. A procedure is presented that adapts unitarity methods to the computation of Magnus amplitudes.

entry.title: Multigroup Radiation Diffusion with Compton Scattering on a Moving Mesh: Implementation in RICH and Application to Tidal Disruption Events
entry.summary: Compton scattering exchanges energy between radiation and hot gas and changes the spectrum in high-energy astrophysical systems such as tidal disruption events (TDEs). Because it couples all photon energies and can act faster than the hydrodynamic time step, many radiation-hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations omit its spectral redistribution or treat its energy exchange in the gray approximation. We extend the multigroup flux-limited diffusion module of the moving-mesh RHD code RICH to include Compton scattering with the exact thermal Compton kernel. In our semi-implicit scheme for the thermal radiative transfer equation, the temperature dependence of the kernel enters a generalized Fleck factor, and the group Compton operator conserves photon number and satisfies detailed balance. In equilibration tests, the scheme agrees with independent solutions, relaxes without absorption and emission to a Bose-Einstein spectrum, and remains stable for time steps that do not resolve the Compton equilibration timescale. We apply it to a three-dimensional simulation of the disruption of a $0.5\,M_\odot$ star by a $10^6\,M_\odot$ black hole. We find that during the X-ray flash, inverse Compton scattering dominates the coupling between the gas and the radiation near the nozzle shock, where it adds X-ray energy much faster than thermal emission and may affect the dynamics. Outside the X-ray thermalization radii, its instantaneous X-ray production rate during the flash is comparable to or larger than the escaping X-ray luminosity, so it may contribute substantially to the X-ray emission from TDEs.
entry.arxiv:comment: 27 pages, 16 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to ApJS

entry.title: Segre determinants and MHV gravity amplitudes
entry.summary: We describe a Segre-Veronese construction of polynomial solutions to the interpolation conditions of the numerators of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes given by Hodges' formula. The five- and six-point Hodges numerators arise from Segre determinants, while for every $n\geq7$ suitable Segre determinants lead to solutions linearly independent of the Hodges numerator. The existence of such independent elements for $n=7,8$ was recently established by Mai and Zhang.

entry.title: Charmed baryon-to-meson ratios inside jets as a discriminator of hadronization mechanisms: from color reconnection in p+p to coalescence in Pb+Pb
entry.summary: Jets separate the products of hard scatterings from the underlying event and thus help to clarify the origin of the enhanced baryon-to-meson ratios observed from small to large collision systems. We investigate the charmed baryon-to-meson ratio $Λ_c^+/D^0$ within jets in p+p and Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$~TeV to discriminate between candidate hadronization mechanisms. In p+p collisions, simulated with PYTHIA8 using color reconnection (CR-BLC Mode 2) as a representative beyond-leading-color scenario, the in-jet ratio is enhanced at low-to-intermediate $p_T$ relative to the inclusive one---opposite to the light-flavor $Λ/K^0_S$ case---because the color-reconnection-induced excess of the ratio remains correlated with the jet and survives the jet requirement, while the fragmentation baseline shows no such enhancement. In Pb+Pb collisions, described by the SHELL model with a coalescence plus fragmentation hybrid hadronization, the in-jet ratio is instead suppressed moderately at intermediate $p_T$, because coalescence hadrons assembled from soft thermal partons carry no correlation with the jet direction and are preferentially discarded by the jet selection. The sign of the in-jet modification thus discriminates between the two mechanisms. Both mechanisms shift charmed hadrons toward small values of the parallel jet momentum fraction $z^{ch}_{||}$, with a stronger effect on $Λ_c^+$, so that the $z^{ch}_{||}$ spectrum probes non-fragmentation hadronization independently of parton energy loss. The radial profile of the in-jet ratio rises with the distance from the jet axis in both systems, with the lowest-$p_T$ interval displaced farthest for color reconnection and the intermediate-$p_T$ interval for coalescence. These results provide the baseline and predictions needed for future jet-tagged charmed-hadron measurements in both collision systems.

entry.title: Linear causality and stability constraints on relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics
entry.summary: In this work, we construct a theoretical framework for relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics based on entropy current analysis. The formalism consistently incorporates finite relaxation dynamics of the dissipative fluxes, providing a transient framework suitable for analyzing linear stability and short-wavelength causality. Utilizing linear mode analysis, we investigate the constraints imposed by causality and stability on this anisotropic system. By linearizing the theory around a homogeneous equilibrium state, we identify the magnetosonic, Alfvén, and charge-diffusion sectors, together with their coupling terms. For each sector, we derive asymptotic dispersion relations in both the long-wavelength (small-$k$) and short-wavelength (large-$k$) regimes, validating them against exact numerical roots. Our numerical analysis confirms the accuracy of these asymptotic solutions and uncovers a nontrivial angular dependence, especially near special propagation directions where the ordinary momentum expansion becomes less reliable. By evaluating the large-$k$ behavior of the propagating branches alongside the damping properties of non-hydrodynamic modes, we delineate the corresponding causality constraints. We find that the admissible linear causal domain is governed by the interplay between propagation direction, anisotropic transport coefficients, and relaxation times, with the resulting bounds being intrinsically mode-dependent. These findings provide a systematic theoretical basis for investigating linear stability and short-wavelength causality in relativistic magnetohydrodynamics beyond the first-order approximation.

entry.title: Fewer simulations, sharper covariances: Reducing mock covariance noise with Zeldovich approximation control variates
entry.summary: We present a control-variate method for reducing the variance of power spectrum covariance matrix estimates from simulations of large-scale structure. The idea is to pair each mock simulation with a cheap Zeldovich-approximation realization sharing the same initial conditions, and to use the known statistical properties of the Zeldovich field to remove correlated sample variance from the covariance estimator. Under a Gaussian disconnected approximation, we derive fully analytic expressions for both the optimal control-variate coefficient, $β(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, and the corresponding correlation, $ρ(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, in terms of the auto- and cross-power spectra of the target and control fields. In the monopole case, the correlation takes the simple form $ρ(k,k') = r^2(k),r^2(k')$, where $r(k)$ is the standard cross-correlation coefficient between the target and Zeldovich fields, implying that covariance estimation remains highly efficient whenever the two fields are strongly correlated. For masked redshift-space lognormal mocks, resembling LRGs from DESI, we find that the control-variate estimator reduces the variance of the covariance matrix by approximately an order of magnitude on large scales, $k\lesssim 0.05\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, precisely where accurate covariance estimation is most challenging. The gains are smaller for higher $k$ but typically accelerate convergence by a factor of 2-3, substantially lowering the computational cost of covariance estimation for current and upcoming large-scale structure surveys. After a cheap parametric-bootstrap calibration of the precision-matrix bias, the control-variate covariance yields a $χ^2$ distribution consistent with the expected number of degrees of freedom. This method is readily implementable in current imaging and spectroscopic surveys (e.g., DESI, \textit{Euclid}, LSST, PFS, \textit{SPHEREx}).

entry.title: Breaking the symmetry: X-ray polarization from a spreading layer on a tilted weakly magnetized neutron star
entry.summary: When modeling the emission from an X-ray binary system, we often assume that the rotational axis of the compact object is aligned with that of the binary system. While often considered irrelevant for spectroscopic observations, the orientation of the binary system is crucial for polarimetric properties. With the recent advent of X-ray polarimetric observations enabled by the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), indications of a possible misalignment of the neutron star rotational axis with respect to the binary axis have been reported. Following these indications, we present an analytical model for the polarimetric properties of emission arising from a spreading layer on an inclined weakly magnetized neutron star (WMNS). We discuss the expected polarimetric properties and study the impact of geometrical parameters of the system on the polarization of WMNS emission. We compare our results with those for aligned systems. Finally, we discuss applications of the model to recent and upcoming X-ray polarimetric observations with IXPE and mention the suggestions for further development of the model.

entry.title: Exact stress-tensor generators distinguish integrable continuations
entry.summary: The same leading $T\bar T$ interaction can coexist with sharply different strong-field responses, even within causal, classically integrable sigma models. We reconstruct exact autonomous stress-tensor generators for prescribed one-scale Courant--Hilbert families in two dimensions. Separating the invariant stress scale from a signed trace ratio reduces reconstruction to one scalar inversion on each invertible physical branch. The resulting profile determines both the deformation law and the relation between local energy density and pressure. For generalized Born--Infeld and logarithmic models, the leading interactions coincide, yet pressure saturates in the former and grows without bound in the latter. Their exact generators are respectively quadratic and nonpolynomial, the latter involving Lambert $W_{-1}$. A regular Legendre transformation gives the same profile in the auxiliary potential formulation. The flows commute locally with root-$T\bar T$ within a common smooth branch and retain a common classical Lax form. Exact reconstruction thus quantifies the nonlinear freedom left by leading-order matching.

entry.title: A class of decelerating inhomogeneous cosmological models giving rise to accelerating FLRW universes at large scales
entry.summary: In this manuscript, we develop a class of inhomogeneous relativistic cosmological models with the following properties: (i) They contain cosmological observers to whom the spatial geometry and the expansion are homogeneous and isotropic; (ii) Matter behaves closely to dust, as it is formed by an ensemble of massive particles whose number density $4$-vector is conserved and reacts viscously to the local tidal forces; (iii) They generalize the dust FLRW model; (iv) They give rise to effective models on large scales that reproduce the FLRW behaviour with dust and a running dark-energy term, which appears as a backreaction effect from the local gravitational potential; (v) By suitably setting the distribution of energy in the current universe, the effective large-scale equation-of-state parameter can reproduce, in principle, any polynomial on the scale factor whose term of order zero is negative; (vi) The luminous distance observations imply an apparent large-scale acceleration, as the deceleration parameter is negative, while in reality the universe is decelerating.

entry.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
entry.summary: Monodromy (twist) line defects arise as the boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, which are among the simplest non-trivial conformal defects with direct realizations as magnetic vortex in quantum magnets, as Wilson and t Hooft lines of gauge theories, and as the replica twist operators in quantum information theory. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we design a way to realize the monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), $π$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $π$-twist and the reflection). For each defect, we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the surrounding critical bulk. Among the low-lying defect primaries resolved in our spectra, we find no relevant scalar perturbation that preserves all the symmetries of the corresponding defect. The relevant deformations identified in our calculations break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist. Our construction therefore turns the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization, opening a route to exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.

entry.title: Exact WKB analysis of inverted triple-well: resonance, PT-symmetry breaking, and resurgence
entry.summary: We study non-Hermitian quantum mechanics of an inverted triple-well potential within the exact WKB framework. For a single classical potential, different Siegert boundary conditions define three distinct quantum problems: the PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance systems. For each case, we derive the exact quantization condition and construct the associated trans-series solution. By identifying the resurgent structures and cancellations in these non-Hermitian setups, we obtain the median-summed series, clarifying when the spectra are real or complex in accordance with the physical properties of each system. Establishing explicit links to the semi-classical path integral formalism, we elucidate the roles of bounce and bion configurations in these non-Hermitian systems. This analysis predicts PT-symmetry breaking, which we also verify numerically. Using the median quantization conditions, we prove the existence of this symmetry breaking and establish an exact equation for the exceptional point, which emerges as a remarkably simple algebraic relation between the bounce and bion actions. We further show that the median-summed non-perturbative correction to the spectrum vanishes at the exceptional point, while the resurgent structure survives through a universal minimal trans-series. For the resonance and anti-resonance systems, we find that the exact median-summed spectra are related by complex conjugation, representing time reversal in this setting, are necessarily complex, and do not exhibit an exceptional point. Although their spectra differ significantly from the PT-symmetric case, they share the same minimal trans-series. By maintaining explicit links with the path integral saddles and the formal theory of resurgence, our analysis provides a unified and general perspective on the quantization of non-Hermitian theories.

entry.title: High precision black hole scattering
entry.summary: In this thesis we compute the impulse of a classical black hole scattering encounter in the Post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion - a weak-field expansion in Newton's constant $G$ - up to the fifth order. We describe the black holes as point particles within an effective field theory framework and couple them through gravity. The classical equations of motion are solved diagrammatically using the worldline quantum field theory (WQFT) formalism, in which the solution with causal boundary conditions is encoded in tree-level Feynman diagrams built from graviton and worldline fields. The Feynman integrals arising at each order are reduced by advanced IBP reduction techniques and evaluated with the method of differential equations. We find that, in the solution of these integrals, periods over Calabi--Yau manifolds - familiar from string theory - appear and contribute to the classical impulse at the fifth Post-Minkowskian order. The results of this work are the first analytic results for the scattering observables at fifth Post-Minkowskian order, together with the appearance of Calabi--Yau threefold periods in a classical physics observable.

entry.title: Exact few-magnon Bethe scars of the non-integrable alternating Heisenberg chain
entry.summary: Exact solutions of quantum lattice models serve as useful guides for interpreting physical phenomena in condensed matter systems. Prominent examples of integrability appear in one dimension, including the Heisenberg chain, where the Bethe ansatz method has been widely successful. Recent work has noted that certain non-integrable models harbor quantum many-body scar states, which form a superspin of regular states hidden in an otherwise chaotic spectrum. Here we consider one of the simplest examples of a non-integrable model, the alternating ferromagnetic-antiferromagnetic (bond-staggered) Heisenberg chain, a close cousin of the spin-1 Haldane chain and a spin analog of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, and show the presence of exponentially many zero-energy states. We highlight features of the alternating chain that allow treatment with the coordinate Bethe ansatz (with important modifications), and surprisingly, for a non-integrable system, we find simple compact expressions for zero-energy eigenfunctions for a few magnons, including solutions with fractionalized particle momentum. These states exhibit wavefunction scarring similar to that of single-particle states in chaotic billiards. We discuss a general numerical recipe to diagnose the existence of such generalized Bethe ansatz (GBA) scar states and also provide exact analytic expressions for their entanglement. We conclude by conjecturing a picture of magnon pairing which may generalize to multiple magnons. Our work opens the avenue to describe certain eigenstates of partially integrable systems using the GBA.

entry.title: In Search of the Gravitational Wave of Fast X-Ray Transient in the Second Part of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Fourth Observing Run
entry.summary: Fast X-ray Transients (FXTs) are brief, intense X-ray flashes unassociated with persistent X-ray sources or known stellar objects, typically lasting from seconds to hours. With the launch of the Einstein Probe in January 2024, the study of FXTs has entered a new phase. Its large field of view significantly increases the discovery rate, enabling more robust statistics. The leading discoveries have revealed a fraction of gamma-ray bursts, while the rest remain unexplained. We propose a methodology to search for possible relations between gravitational waves (GWs) and FXTs, as it may serve as a discrepancy among proposed theoretical models. To achieve this, we intend to utilize X-Pipeline, an unmodeled search algorithm, to identify excess coherent signals in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) O4b observations. Out of 64 FXTs events, we obtained 19 FXTs for constructing robust searches. Given the absence of any detectable GW signals, we subsequently calculated upper limits and estimated exclusion distances for each source. In order to enrich the sample base and statistical analysis, this methodology could henceforth be conducted through future GW searches, including KAGRA in the O4c and O5 observations.

entry.title: Clarifications on black/white hole metastable relics as dark matter
entry.summary: The idea that the evaporation of black holes could end around the Planck mass and lead to relics possibly accounting for dark matter is quite old. In this article we focus on new models where the relics are metastable, typically with a lifetime of order $M^5$, where $M$ is the initial mass of the black hole. We show that those relics would actually be quite luminous, radiating -- possibly as much as the stars -- in the optical or UV band. We explicitly construct a proposal for their direct detection.

entry.title: Four-dimensional supersymmetric massive QED
entry.summary: We study a four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric Proca model with an explicit mass term for a real vector superfield and a generalized transverse kinetic operator. Although it displays no gauge redundancy in Proca variables, for local kinetic operators the model is the exact classical unitary-gauge form of the minimal Abelian $\mathcal N=1$ Stueckelberg realization, with the SQED-like exponential as its minimal gauge-covariant matter coupling. We compute the Kählerian contribution to the one-loop effective action using both the background-field Hessian and an independent supergraph organization. In the minimal model the background-dependent divergence is local and is absorbed by the matter Kähler normalization, and the finite local terms left by the subtraction remain scheme dependent. At $α=0$, an anomaly-free minimal Stueckelberg formulation supports a conditional perturbative-renormalizability interpretation for the corresponding minimal theory. For $f(\Box)=\Box+α\Box^2$ we distinguish the exact polynomial model, defined over the full momentum range, from a truncated derivative expansion; in the latter reading, the additional pole and the local matching term are ultraviolet information determined by the completion rather than predictions of the truncated theory.
entry.arxiv:comment: 36 pages, accepted to Nuclear Physics B

entry.title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
entry.summary: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.

entry.title: Radial Stability of Charged Interacting Quark Stars Revisited
entry.summary: An error in the charged quark star literature \cite{Goncalves:2020joq} has resulted in erroneous solutions to the radial stability equations for charged interacting quark stars in \cite{zhang:2021}. In this article we recalculate the fundamental radial eigenfrequencies for charged, interacting quark stars in general relativity and discuss any departure from previous results \cite{zhang:2021}. Most of the qualitative trends persist, but the magnitudes of the separation between the maximum mass and stability points on a given branch can change significantly. We also note that all branches in \cite{zhang:2021} that contained no stable solutions now have stable solutions in their corrected counterparts. The net effect is that in all of the studied cases charged quark stars have a greater range of stability than originally predicted. We also compare four recent observational constraints not included in previous studies, and find that these constraints are satisfied by a subset of the mass-radius relations we obtain.

entry.title: Effective field equations with stochastic initial conditions
entry.summary: The evolution of quantum field expectation values from an initial non-equilibrium quantum state can be followed numerically using the Truncated Wigner technique. It can track non-perturbative quantum phenomena, such as false vacuum decay, in real time with promising results. Nevertheless, it is an approximate method subject to quantum loop corrections. The extension of Truncated Wigner into a fully fledged effective field equation approach is discussed here, including corrections from higher loops and higher momenta.

entry.title: Ongoing and Post-Mass-Transfer Binaries: A Living Catalog and Unified Review of Binary Mass Transfer Products
entry.summary: Mass transfer is arguably the most defining interaction in binary stellar systems, yet many aspects of its physics remain poorly understood, from stability to endpoints and observable products. Comparing theory and observations is challenging because post-mass-transfer systems are studied across largely independent communities with different methods, nomenclature, and evolutionary frameworks. % We present a unified review and catalog of ongoing and post-mass-transfer binaries spanning the full stellar mass range, but restricted to systems likely to have experienced only a single episode of mass transfer (i.e., only one component is evolved). We review 16 observational classes of binary interaction products and compile a curated sample of 5,452 systems into a publicly available, community-driven catalog at https://binary-observations.github.io/post_mt_catalog/. % Using this catalog, we investigate global trends in orbital periods, eccentricities, masses, and mass ratios across post-mass-transfer binaries. We find I) non-zero eccentricities are common at all periods and system classes, with both median values and scatter increasing with period, II) the $e(\log P)$ relation depends on donor progenitor mass, with neutron-star and black-hole binaries showing the highest median eccentricities, likely reflecting effects of natal kicks, III) period distributions are broad and overlapping across evolutionary channels, and IV) the Gaia BH and NS systems are extreme in mass ratio but otherwise consistent with the general post-mass-transfer population. Together, these results support a unified empirical view of post-mass-transfer binaries that highlights several tensions between theory and observations.

entry.title: String Amplitudes on Integer Rectangles
entry.summary: Hidden zeros of tree-level string amplitudes of colored scalars lie on loci specified by integer-valued dimensionless momentum contractions arranged in rectangles on the kinematic mesh. We study the same kinematic loci for open-string amplitudes with gluons, fermions and higher-spin states at arbitrary finite mass levels. Disk monodromy relations yield $\textit{zero-locus factorization}$: at regular points where the monodromy system is invertible, the amplitude is a weighted sum of physical three-point amplitudes sewn to complete on-shell $(n-1)$-point amplitudes. Hidden zeros follow when the external wavefunctions annihilate all contributing three-point couplings. In the low-energy limit, the massless zero-integer branch recovers the corresponding field-theory factorization. For closed strings, including gravitons, persistent cubic zeros in both chiral sectors remove the disk poles, allowing the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye momentum-kernel zero to imply amplitude zeros. The operator product expansions of external vertices give a common worldsheet origin for these conditions across spins and mass levels.

entry.title: Spin-resolved microscopy of $^{87}$Sr SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard systems
entry.summary: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin-1/2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU($N$) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU($N$) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic $^{87}$Sr. Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the 10 spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin-9/2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish $^{87}$Sr quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard model, and provide a new detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.

entry.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
entry.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

entry.title: Holographic surface defect RG flows without supersymmetry
entry.summary: We consider $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory with gauge group SU$(N)$, which admits families of conformal surface defects defined by singular boundary conditions for scalar fields that completely break supersymmetry. At large $N$ and strong coupling, these defects are holographically dual either to a probe D5-brane or to one of two new D7-brane embeddings that we introduce in this work. We also construct embeddings of both D5- and D7-branes describing defect renormalisation group (RG) flows, for which the ultraviolet and infrared fixed points are both dual to the same D$p$-brane, with different values of a parameter. Our embeddings dual to RG flows are mostly constructed numerically, but we find a regime in which we can derive approximate analytic embeddings using a controlled perturbative expansion. We demonstrate that the $b$-theorem is satisfied by all of the RG flows that we study.

entry.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
entry.summary: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.

entry.title: The XMM-Newton view of the DEM L36 superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
entry.summary: We present the first multi-wavelength analysis of the DEM L36 superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud. We compare the DEM L36 superbubble with other Galactic and Magellanic Cloud superbubbles. We use data from XMM-Newton, supplemented by data from the Magellanic Cloud Emission Line Survey, the Dark Energy Camera Magellanic Cloud Emission Line Survey, the Spitzer Space Telescope, and the Australia Telescope Compact Array. We perform a multi-wavelength morphological analysis to understand the shape and structure of the superbubble and X-ray spectral analysis to derive physical parameters of the hot gas. We find significant X-ray emission in DEM L36, dominated by a central bubble region mostly confined by a thin H$α$ filamentary shell. This has two distinct blowout regions to the east and west, with a possible smaller blowout in the south. Spectral analysis shows the X-ray emission is well fit with a thermal plasma model in collisional ionisation equilibrium with a temperature of $kT=0.17~(0.16-0.18)$ keV and unabsorbed luminosity $L_{X~(0.5-7.0~\mathrm{keV})}=3.62\times 10^{35} $erg s$^{-1}$. Unlike other LMC superbubbles, we find no clear powering cluster at the centre, though relatively small clusters near the edge are likely supplying the mechanical input at the present epoch. We use photometric data of these clusters to estimate cluster masses, ages, and mechanical inputs to compare with the energy stored in the superbubble. We find that these clusters have supplied more energy over their lifetime than is currently observed in the superbubble, indicative of the so-called growth rate discrepancy problem. It is likely the DEM L36 superbubble was initially shaped by a central massive stellar population that has since dispersed and largely lost to supernovae, with smaller clusters at the edges of the swept-up shell being currently supplying the energy input.
entry.arxiv:comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, accepted by Astronomy & Astrophysics

entry.title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
entry.summary: The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder. We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat $Λ$CDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly. We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered $H_0$ from $74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20}$ to $71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the forward analysis and from $60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97}$ to $63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint. Comparing the cosmological intercepts of the magnitude-redshift relation inferred from two rungs of the distance ladder before and after peculiar-velocity corrections, we find that the significance of the discrepancy decreases from $6.8σ$ to $3.9σ$ in the forward check and from $7.3σ$ to $4.3σ$ in the backward check. Peculiar-velocity corrections therefore partially alleviate the intercept tension, while a residual discrepancy persists within the adopted framework. Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.

entry.title: Gravitational waves from highly charged binary black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory
entry.summary: We perform fully nonlinear numerical-relativity simulations of electrically charged binary black hole mergers in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMD) theory, varying the magnitude and relative sign of the input charges and the dilaton coupling $a$. In the weak-charge sequence, the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to the neutral vacuum baseline of general relativity and are visually indistinguishable across the sampled couplings, consistent with earlier EMD simulations. For the highly charged binaries with equal-magnitude opposite charges, however, the dominant gravitational strain exhibits visible differences between the EMD cases with $a\neq0$ and the charged Einstein-Maxwell reference at $a=0$. At $a=1$, the coordinate-time interval from the same separation to the waveform-based merger is approximately $62\%$ shorter than for the neutral binary. In this high-charge sequence at fixed input charges, increasing $a$ strengthens the scalar dressing while leaving the individual dilaton-weighted horizon charges nearly unchanged. Within the same sequence, increasing $a$ across the sampled values decreases the dipolar electromagnetic-flux peak, increases the scalar-flux peak, and modestly lengthens the merger interval. The sampled like-charged binaries have corresponding merger intervals approximately $15\%$-$20\%$ longer than the neutral baseline and emit predominantly quadrupolar electromagnetic radiation. At $a=1$ and $a=\sqrt{3}$, the like-charged mergers leave charged remnants with scalar fields consistent with secondary dilaton hair. The opposite-charge remnants instead approach neutral black holes without stationary scalar hair.

entry.title: Robust paths to primordial $B$ modes in the presence of polarised point source contamination
entry.summary: A detection of primordial $B$ modes in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarisation relies on a robust control and removal of contamination from astrophysical polarised foreground emission. We examine how much polarised extragalactic point sources may contaminate the cosmological signal in ground-based CMB experiments, propagating their impact through component separation to the final parameter constraints. We discuss masking and modelling strategies to ensure that the resulting constraints remain both accurate and precise under this source of contamination. We produce synthetic data containing polarised emission from extragalactic radio sources (ERSs) and dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) following state-of-the-art models for both samples. We find that, while the DSFG contribution is likely too small to cause any significant bias to the cosmological or foreground parameters, the ERS contribution instead, if left unmasked, leads to a bias in the parameters describing the Galactic synchrotron and lensing $B$-mode components. For experiments targeting noise levels of order $σ_P\simeq 1\,μK\,{\rm arcmin}$, we find that masking all ERSs with fluxes above $\sim$0.1 Jy, coupled with a relatively simple model to marginalise over residual point-source contamination, achieves a suitable balance that allows for the robust recovery of unbiased cosmological and foreground parameters at a negligible cost in parameter uncertainties.

entry.title: Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent
entry.summary: We propose Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent (QCHD), a continuous-time quantum framework for optimization under smooth equality constraints. The unconstrained counterpart, Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD), minimizes a cost function by simulating the Schrödinger dynamics of a particle in the potential given by the cost function. Applying Dirac's formalism to the classical dynamics with constraints, we construct an intrinsic quantum Hamiltonian with a Laplace--Beltrami operator on the constraint manifold in a kinetic term. Its evolution preserves the constraints exactly without penalty terms and is expected to solve quantum-dynamically the constrained optimization problem. We analyze its relation to Quantum Hamiltonian Descent supplemented by a strong penalty term. For a squared-distance penalty, the effective tangential dynamics acquires an extrinsic-curvature potential and, in nontrivial normal-rotation sectors, a coupling to the normal-bundle connection. These embedding-dependent terms remain in the strong-penalty limit, generally yielding quantum dynamics different from QCHD. Numerical comparisons for circular, elliptical, and two simultaneous constraints show faster optimization and improved concentration near global minima for the initial states and finite penalty strengths considered.

entry.title: Integral representations of quantum Rényi divergences on von Neumann algebras
entry.summary: We prove an integral representation of the $α$-$z$ Rényi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=cα$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $α$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the Rényi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $α$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.

entry.title: A cosmic filament catalog for COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 across 0.5 < z < 3.5
entry.summary: Cosmic filaments represent the environments in which most galaxies form and evolve. However, the spatial distribution of filaments and the link between galaxy properties and their positions relative to filaments remains unclear, particularly at high redshifts. In this work, using the deep-field catalog COSMOS-Web Data Release 1, we construct a filament catalog spanning 0.5 < z < 3.5 that can be directly applied to studies of galaxy evolution and the galaxy--large-scale-structure connection at the peak epoch of galaxy and black hole formation. We developed a new procedure based on the DisPerSE method that fully incorporates the probability distribution functions (PDFs) of galaxy photometric redshifts by generating multiple realizations for each tomographic 2D slice. We then stacked these realizations to construct ``filament probability maps'' (w_ fil maps), from which filaments were subsequently extracted. The filament extraction parameters were optimized using mock catalogs generated from TNG simulations by minimizing the discrepancies between 3D and projected 2D filaments. Applying this procedure to the COSMOS-Web data, we detected 12,523 filaments (comprising 136,210 segments) across 0.5 < z < 3.5 and released a filament catalog, a companion segment catalog, and filament probability maps for each slice. Validation against astrophysical properties shows a strong agreement between the extracted filaments and those in the simulations, supporting the robustness of the filament extraction. These data products provide a robust foundation for investigating galaxy--environment coevolution at cosmic noon and beyond.

entry.title: Identifying galactic binary systems of neutron stars and black holes with LISA
entry.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect $\sim 100$ galactic binary systems comprised of black holes and neutron stars. Distinguishing these binaries from the $\sim 10^4$ double white dwarfs detectable by LISA will be challenging. In the absence of any other information, the inferred component masses can be used to classify the nature of these objects. However, short-period galactic binaries $\sim 10^7$--$10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$ from coalescence produce a quasi-monochromatic signal which carries little information about their masses. We generate synthetic LISA data sets containing gravitational waves from Galactic binary black holes, binary neutron stars and black hole-neutron stars drawn from an astrophysically realistic population produced through the isolated binary evolution channel. We use a Bayesian inference pipeline to explore the accuracy with which the component masses can be measured. LISA will be able to infer component masses for $\approx 10\% - 50\%$ of the detected systems by measuring the orbital eccentricity, periapse precession frequency, and gravitational-wave induced frequency derivative. Typical fractional mass errors are $\approx 1\%$--$100\%$ (depending on the specific value of the source parameters) enabling the classification of the constituent objects as black holes or neutron stars. For these binaries, LISA will also be able to determine their 3-dimensional position in the Milky Way. LISA detections of these double compact objects will provide new insights to their astrophysical formation processes, the Galactic population, and the Milky Way's star formation history. However, for a significant fraction of the LISA-detected binaries the nature of their constituent objects may remain unclear.

entry.title: Many-body localization
entry.summary: We present an introductory review of nonergodic dynamics in interacting many-body quantum systems, focusing on the phenomenon of many-body localization (MBL). We describe aspects of MBL and summarize the evidence for a crossover from the ergodic to the MBL regime in finite systems, using the paradigmatic XXZ model as an example. We then broaden the scope to other models to illustrate the generality of the phenomenon. We briefly touch on the largely unexplored relation between MBL and quantum computing.

entry.title: Exploring the connection between Fast Radio Bursts and binary neutron star mergers
entry.summary: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are highly energetic radio sources whose duration is of the order of milliseconds. The physical origin of these sources is still unknown. Many models suggest magnetars as possible progenitors of FRBs, and this is supported by the association between FRBs and the Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154; other proposed progenitors include binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, that are themselves linked to magnetar formation. In this work we investigate the possible connection between FRBs and BNS mergers, including magnetars that might be produced in such events, by comparing the detection rates inferred from synthetic BNS and associated FRB populations with the rates observed by CHIME. We produce a synthetic catalog of BNS mergers by combining recent theoretically predicted BNS merger rate as a function of redshift and the neutron star mass distribution inferred from measurements of Galactic BNSs. Using this catalog we predict the number of BNS systems ending as magnetars (stable or supramassive neutron star) or black holes (formed promptly or after the collapse of a hypermassive neutron star) for different equations of state. We then simulate for each BNS (and therefore for each magnetar remnant) an associated FRB and estimate how many of them can be potentially detected by CHIME. We find that the rate of BNS mergers and the rate of magnetars produced after BNS represents a non-negligible fraction of the FRBs detected by CHIME, both repeating and non-repeating. Although additional formation channels need to be considered to account for the entire population of FRBs, the existence of a fraction of FRBs that might genuinely be associated to BNS mergers has profound implications in the context of multi- messenger astronomy, supporting the systematic searches of coincident detections of FRBs and GWs from a BNS merger with current and future facilities.

entry.title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
entry.summary: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.

entry.title: Efficient Eccentric and Quasicircular Effective-One-Body Waveforms via Near-Identity Averaging Transformations
entry.summary: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer, will require accurate and efficient models of long-lived, eccentric black-hole binary signals. In previous work, we reduced the cost of evolving nonspinning eccentric effective-one-body dynamics by recasting the equations of motion in terms of osculating orbital elements and applying near-identity averaging transformations to remove the fast orbital-timescale structure during the inspiral. However, the parametrization in terms of the eccentricity and relativistic anomaly becomes singular in the circular-orbit limit, excluding quasicircular binaries and the late stages of eccentric inspirals. Moreover, the cost of generating the waveform from the averaged dynamics limited the overall speed-up to a factor of $1.5-8$. In this work, we replace the eccentricity and relativistic anomaly by the Cartesian components of the eccentricity vector, in which the averaged equations are regular for all eccentricities $0 \leq e < 1$. We also decompose the waveform modes into radial harmonics whose coefficients are tabulated as functions of the averaged variables, so that the waveform is assembled directly on the output time grid at a fixed cost per sample. We validate the method against the full effective-one-body evolution across the parameter space of binaries observable by ground-based detectors, now including circular orbits. At second postadiabatic order, the waveforms reach median mismatches of $\sim 10^{-8}$ with a maximum of $1.1 \times 10^{-5}$, while achieving speed-ups of $3-100 \times$ on a single core or up to $300 \times$ on eight cores against the serial EOB waveform. Given the speed-ups demonstrated here, we plan to apply these techniques to state-of-the-art SEOBNR models in future work.

entry.title: Quasinormal modes of Type I perturbations of dilaton-Euler-Heisenberg black holes
entry.summary: We study the type I quasinormal modes (QNMs) of magnetically charged dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg (dEH) black holes, where axial gravitational and polar electromagnetic perturbations are coupled. Direct integration and Chebyshev pseudospectral methods give consistent QNM frequencies for the fundamental branches continued from Schwarzschild at $\ell=1,2,3$. Varying $α$ at fixed $ζ=α-β$ changes the spectrum on the same background. The damping response depends on charge and multipole and can have opposite signs for the two coupled branches. For $ζ<0$, dipole damping decreases with charge toward horizon merger. For $ζ>0$, the Type I charge range extends beyond the complementary polarization's local angular-gradient bound. All tracked modes remain damped in the nonextremal ranges, supporting the stability of these branches.

entry.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
entry.summary: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

entry.title: Saxion Decay and Dark Radiation in the KSVZ Axion Model
entry.summary: We calculate the relativistic axion energy density produced by the decay of a curvature-displaced Peccei--Quinn condensate in a quartic KSVZ model. We follow the radial PQ field (the saxion) as it relaxes from its inflationary minimum and determine the surviving condensate abundance from the adiabatic action of its oscillations. We then evolve the condensate through its decay into axions and visible particles to calculate the resulting dark-radiation contribution, expressed as $ΔN_{\rm eff}$. With one heavy coloured KSVZ fermion and no additional portal interactions included, the axion channel dominates the two tree-level decay modes. Two reference histories yield $ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.033$ and $0.12$, with maximum saxion energy fractions below $1\%$ and $4\%$, respectively. At fixed quartic coupling, increasing the duration of curvature release reduces the predicted axion radiation density relative to visible radiation by a factor of approximately $28$ while preserving the primordial isocurvature amplitude.

entry.title: Cosmological Inference with Gravitational-Wave Dark Sirens and 21-cm Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with MeerKAT and SKAO
entry.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) and 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) are emerging as complementary cosmological probes: GWs provide direct luminosity-distance measurements, while neutral-hydrogen (HI) IM traces the matter distribution in redshift space. Their synergy offers a promising avenue for precise measurements of the Hubble constant. Within a standard-siren framework, we perform a joint cosmological and population analysis using $\mathcal{O}(150)$ mock GW detections with SNR > 12, as projected for one year of observations at LVK O5 sensitivity. We combine these with mock HI intensity maps from MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, and study how observational limitations in both the GW and IM data affect the $H_0$ constraints. We find that uncertainty in GW parameter measurements is a dominant limitation on the cosmological constraints. Neglecting this uncertainty, the inclusion of HI information enables sub-percent constraints on $H_0$. We also find that observational effects in the HI surveys weaken the constraints, although they remain tighter than those obtained without HI information (spectral sirens). Despite accounting for HI IM observational limitations, including HI information reduces the $H_0$ uncertainty relative to the spectral-siren results by 61% for MeerKLASS and 53% for SKA-Mid. Because our results are based on a single realisation, they should be interpreted in light of possible realisation-to-realisation variability. Beam convolution most severely weakens the constraints. Instrumental noise can induce multimodality in the posterior, potentially biasing the inferred parameters. The results are sensitive to foreground under-cleaning and over-cleaning. Partial sky coverage has a relatively small impact. In the most realistic scenario, which accounts for both GW and HI IM limitations, we obtain $H_0$ precision estimates of 10% and 15% for MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, respectively.
